problem: Repeated consumer discovery scans every workspace reference for every symbol, making repository audits expensive even when each symbol has few consumers.
subset: Resolved index references and existing definition groups. Preserve exact occurrence order, duplicate occurrences, unresolved matches and confidence. No new resolution or feasible-path claim.
acceptance: Compare cold and repeated consumer queries with an independent linear membership oracle.
Invalidate derived lookups after target changes, name changes, replacement, reordering, insertion, removal and mutable iteration.
Preserve overload groups, cross-language references, ambiguity, Unicode coordinates and source order.
Measure repository and generated workloads before and after, retaining source identities, output sizes, latency and process RSS.
Verify cached resolution, fresh reconstruction, native consumers and the browser feature set.
edit_boundary: Use the fr guide for index discovery. Direct edits implement a mutation-aware reference collection, consumer query APIs, affected native consumers and independent acceptance; no admitted author operation expresses this API and storage change.
claims: Finite query workload speed and memory measurements. No claim that static references include dynamic consumers, that full indexing becomes faster, or that PLAN milestones are complete.
